Section 404(c) of the Rail Passenger Service Act (45 U.S.C. 564(c)), as amended by this Act, is further amended by adding at the end thereof the following new paragraph:


“(5) 
The Route and Service Criteria shall not apply to—

“(A) 
decisions of the Corporation to increase or, where construction schedules, other temporary disruptive factors, or seasonal fluctuations in ridership so warrant, to decrease frequency of service on existing routes or portions of existing routes or on routes where an additional frequency of service is being tested; and


“(B) 
rerouting of service between major population centers on existing routes”.

fable.w: This section only exempts certain Corporation decisions (changes in service frequency and rerouting on existing routes) from the Route and Service Criteria. A tempting reading is that decisions about rail service imply public input, but the text sets out no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. It narrows the scope of the criteria and creates no outside-party process.
fable.s: The Route and Service Criteria shall not apply to—

qwen_block.w: This section defines the scope of applicability for 'Route and Service Criteria' by exempting certain operational decisions made by the Corporation (Amtrak). It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory boards. The text describes internal operational flexibility rather than a mechanism for outside participation in federal decision-making.
qwen_block.s: The Route and Service Criteria shall not apply to— (A) decisions of the Corporation to increase or, where construction schedules, other temporary disruptive factors, or seasonal fluctuations in ridership so warrant, to decrease frequency of service on existing routes or portions of existing routes or on routes where an additional frequency of service is being tested; and (B) rerouting of service between major population centers on existing routes

opus.w: This section only exempts certain Amtrak decisions (changes in how often trains run, and rerouting between major population centers on existing routes) from the Route and Service Criteria. It does not set up any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue for outside parties. One could guess that the criteria themselves once involved outside input, but nothing in this text says so. So the section does not show any participation.
opus.s: The Route and Service Criteria shall not apply to—
opus.b: **Step 1: Analysis.** The tempting reading is that the "Route and Service Criteria" may have involved outside input under the underlying Rail Passenger Service Act, so exempting decisions from them looks like it touches on participation. That reading fails because this section only sets out exemptions: Amtrak's frequency changes and rerouting are excluded from the criteria. It does not create or require any hearing, comment period, consultation, advisory body, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is involved in the decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines exemptions from 'Route and Service Criteria' for specific operational decisions made by the Corporation (Amtrak). It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties (such as the public, states, or local governments) in making these decisions. The text focuses on internal operational flexibility rather than external engagement.
qwen_chat.s: The Route and Service Criteria shall not apply to— (A) decisions of the Corporation to increase or, where construction schedules, other temporary disruptive factors, or seasonal fluctuations in ridership so warrant, to decrease frequency of service on existing routes or portions of existing routes or on routes where an additional frequency of service is being tested; and (B) rerouting of service between major population centers on existing routes
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "decisions of the Corporation" implies a process where the public could participate, or that the exemption from criteria implies a lack of participation. However, the text itself does not mandate or describe any participation mechanism; it merely defines the scope of regulatory criteria. The text is purely definitional/exemptive regarding internal corporate decisions and does not involve outside parties in the decision-making process.
